_meta.note: All 'days out' / window math in each case's notes field is computed against this reference date. If the eval suite is run on a materially different date, window-boundary cases (rr_003, rf_001, cc_002, etc.) should be re-checked against real elapsed time rather than trusted blindly.
_meta.policy_docs_version: return-policy.md and warranty.md as corrected 2026-08-10 — defect timing is now solely governed by warranty.md's 90-day window; return-policy.md's 30-day/14-day windows apply to change-of-mind returns only.
_meta.return_abuse_threshold: 3+ changed_mind returns within a rolling 60-day window. cust_006 currently has 2 (ord_1012 on 2026-07-19, ord_1018 on 2026-07-27) — below threshold. No customer in seed data currently crosses it; cc_002 and cc_011 test correct non-triggering.
_meta.scope: Phase 12 scoped down to two components: triage classification accuracy (exact-match, all 37 non-injection cases) and policy_question answer quality (RAGAS/LLM-as-judge, the 6 pq_ cases remaining after the 2026-08-13 relabeling pass, tagged with policy-qa-golden). Guardrail/injection eval and complex_case resolution/trajectory eval are explicitly out of scope for now — see DECISIONS.md.
_meta.relabeling_pass_2026_08_13: After the first triage-baseline run against vLLM (37 items, several mismatches), Ali reviewed every mismatch directly against the actual system design (ali-as-judge). Six cases were relabeled based on two systemic findings, not one-off fixes: (1) return_request and refund_request nodes perform their own internal policy/eligibility checks (return window, defect coverage, order/return history, stock) — a message requesting an action should stay classified by that action even if eligibility isn't obvious from the text alone, since the downstream node resolves that, not triage. (2) A message with multiple sub-questions that are all resolvable by the same downstream node (e.g. several policy sub-questions answerable via one RAG pass) is a single instance of that intent, not complex_case — complex_case is reserved for sub-asks spanning different nodes or requiring facts not present in the message. Relabeled: cc_011->rr_005 (return_request), cc_007->rr_006 (return_request), cc_002->rr_007 (return_request), pq_006->rr_008 (return_request), cc_008->rf_007 (refund_request), pq_007->cc_013 (complex_case). Two borderline cases (pq_002, pq_003) were reviewed and kept as policy_question. pq_003's phrasing ('can I still get that covered?') is structurally similar to pq_006/rr_008's ('can I still return it?'), which WAS relabeled — this inconsistency is unresolved and flagged for a follow-up decision, not yet reconciled. Intent distribution after relabeling: order_status=4, policy_question=6, return_request=8, refund_request=7, complex_case=9, escalate=3 (total 37, unchanged).
